# Insites

> A hosted application platform. You build on an instance by adding Liquid pages and
> calling controllers that the installed modules already provide.

Read README.md first. Two of the six mechanism pages describe failures that return
HTTP 200, so skimming costs more than reading.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what an instance is, the four traps, the order to build in.
- [Two APIs, two credentials](01-two-apis-two-credentials.md): the module REST API takes
  an instance API key; /api/graph takes a Console CLI token. Neither works on the other,
  and the failure is a bare 401.

## Mechanism

- [Calling a controller](02-calling-a-controller.md): `{% function %}` returns a value,
  `{% include %}` prints and can set your page's HTTP status. Aliases are not file paths.
- [Pages](03-pages.md): create and update pages through `admin_page_create` and
  `admin_page_update`. Filesystem pages do not route.
- [Authorization](04-authorization.md): calling a controller bypasses the policy on the
  REST endpoint that wraps it. Your page carries its own policy or it has none.
- [Storing data](05-storing-data.md): what the modules already store, and when to create
  your own table.
- [Errors and silent failures](06-errors-and-silent-failures.md): errors arrive in the
  return value. Nothing raises.

## Reference

- [Alias inventory](reference/alias-inventory.md): all 404 controller aliases by module.
  Check a name here before calling it.
- [crm/controller/contacts/list](reference/crm-contacts-list.md): a complete contract,
  and the template every other controller reference should follow.

## Not covered

Contracts for the other 403 aliases. Console beyond token minting. Assets, themes and
translations. Ecommerce, events and locator beyond their alias names.
